config.tacz.client.render.auto_select_gu: Auto Filter Gun Smith Table By Held Item

config.tacz.client.render.disable_moveme: Disable all fov effect from the movement speed attribute while holding a gun.
config.tacz.client.render.enable_translu: Should enable translucent while rendering block entity like gunsmith table or statue. Enable this option will result in ADDITIONAL PERFORMANCE OVERHEAD.
config.tacz.client.resource.enable_lazy_: Build heavy client assets such as models and animation state machines on demand. Inventory items are pre-warmed in the background when possible.
config.tacz.client.sound.hit_sound_concu: Max active hit feedback sounds for the same entity and sound id. 0 disables this limit.
config.tacz.client.sound.default_sound_c: Max active normal gun sounds for the same entity and sound id. 0 disables this limit.
config.tacz.client.sound.high_frequency_: Max active high-frequency gun sounds, such as shooting and animation keyframe sounds, for the same entity and sound id. 0 disables this limit.
config.tacz.client.sound.first_person_an: Use a non-relative entity-tracking world sound source for first-person animation keyframe sounds. This can improve compatibility with physical sound mods, but may introduce slight stereo drift while moving.
config.tacz.client.zoom.screen_distance_: Screen distance coefficient for zoom, using MDV standard, default is MDV133
config.tacz.client.zoom.zoom_sensitivity: Zoom sensitivity is multiplied by this factor

config.tacz.client.render.enable_tooltip: Display the gun/ammo/attachment id in item tooltip when advanced tooltip(F3+H) is on.
Whether or not apply fadeout effect on the laser beam. Close this may improve laser performance under some shaders.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_enab: Enable picture-in-picture optic magnification. Keeps the outside view at 1x while magnifying the target inside the scope lens.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_min_: Only use picture-in-picture when the scope's current zoom level is at least this value; weaker optics fall back to classic full-screen zoom. Low-power scopes (2x-3x) look fine with full-screen zoom, and skipping PIP saves its per-frame cost. Variable scopes are judged by the currently selected zoom level. 1.0 = PIP for every scope.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_rere: Render the world a second time with a narrow FOV for native resolution (helps 6x-8x optics). Off uses screen re-projection with near-zero overhead. EXPERIMENTAL: drives the level renderer twice per frame.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_reso: Second-render mode only, without shader packs. Render resolution scale (0.25 to 1.0, default 0.75 = ~56% pixels). Under shader packs use 'PIP Shader Shadow Scale' instead.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_shad: Shadow map resolution fraction for the scope pass under shader packs (0.25 to 1.0). Default 0.5 cuts that pass’s shadow cost to about a quarter without affecting the main view.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_rere: Rerender mode only: actually render the scope world pass every N frames, reusing the previous lens image in between (1 = every frame). The main lever under shaders, where the cost comes from running the whole shader pipeline twice per frame: 2 halves that extra cost, with about one frame of lens lag while turning. The main view always runs at full frame rate.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_allo: Run the scope picture-in-picture while an Iris shader pack is active. Off by default as a precaution, not because it is known to be broken.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_isol: Give the scope pass its own Iris pipeline so its temporal state cannot corrupt the main view (TAA, clouds, grain).
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_worl: Fraction of the scope magnification handled by the whole screen (0.0 to 1.0). 0 = full PIP (pure optic zoom), 1 = whole-screen FOV zoom.
config.tacz.client.render.scope_pip_shar: Unsharp mask strength for the re-projected lens view (0.0 to 1.0). Cannot invent detail, only recovers apparent crispness.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_enable.de: Master switch for TacZ Mesh Loader poly_mesh rendering. Cube-only rendering is unaffected.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_poly_in_s: Whether to render poly_mesh during shadow passes. Default false: the cube body already provides shadow shapes, and skipping the shadow pass halves the per-frame vertex cost for high-poly guns under shader packs.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_max_rende: Maximum distance (blocks) to render poly_mesh in world contexts (other players, dropped items). 0 = unlimited. First-person view is always rendered in full.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_poly_in_p: Whether to render poly_mesh in GUI/FIXED preview contexts.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_log_stats: Log poly_mesh statistics (bone/vertex counts) when models load.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gui_max_v: Vertex budget for poly_mesh in GUI/FIXED/HEAD. Icons above this budget render cube-only (or the pack LOD model when present). 0 = unlimited.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_world_max: Vertex budget for poly_mesh in third-person / dropped-item / frame contexts. Above this budget only cubes are drawn. 0 = unlimited.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_world_ful: Within this distance (blocks), high-poly mesh guns in the world (third-person, dropped items, item frames, display statues) always render in full detail, ignoring the vertex budget. Without this, dense guns lacking a pack-provided LOD model would vanish to cube-only right in front of you. Beyond this distance the vertex budget applies as usual. 0 = no exemption.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_bakin: Bake first-person poly_mesh gun models into resident GPU buffers, uploading only bone matrices each frame. Massively reduces CPU cost for high-poly (100k+ vertex) mesh guns. World/GUI/dropped items are unaffected. Automatically falls back to the CPU path if the GPU pass fails.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_under: Mesh GPU: Raw Pass Under Shaders (Diagnostic)

With a shader pack, GPU-baked mesh guns normally draw through the vanilla RenderType pipeline so Iris lights them like any other gun. Turn this ON to force the raw GPU pass instead: it bypasses the shader pipeline entirely (gun body gets NO shader lighting). Only useful for diagnosing pack-specific issues with the default route.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_world: Extend GPU baking to guns in the world: third-person guns held by other players, dropped items, item frames and display statues draw from the same resident GPU buffers, uploading only bone matrices per gun per frame. This is what keeps multiplayer playable when many high-poly mesh guns are on screen. Light is handled by a small per-light-level cache (see Light Cache Size). Requires Mesh GPU Baking. Falls back to the CPU path if the GPU pass fails.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_light: Mesh GPU World Light Cache Size

How many quantized light levels of baked world buffers to keep per gun model (LRU). Guns at different light levels in the same scene each need their own baked copy; 4 covers nearly all scenes. Each cached level costs GPU memory proportional to the model's vertex count. First-person baking is unaffected.
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_gpu_bake_: How many world-gun bakes may run in one frame. Prevents evict-rebake thrash when a scene spans more light levels than the cache holds; overflow guns fall back to the CPU path for that frame. Independent of the light cache size (cache = GPU memory, budget = per-frame CPU/upload cost).
config.tacz.client.render.mesh_max_model: Soft warning threshold logged once per geo at load time. Does not change rendering; tells pack authors the model is too dense.
